item.title: Civil Service Commission Monthly Testing Clinics.
item.description:
Interested in a career with the City of Columbus...

 

Register for a Civil Service Commission Testing Clinic!

The City of Columbus employs over 10,000 people in approximately 650+ different job titles.  City employees perform a variety of necessary jobs that help to maintain the quality of life for city residents, such as collecting the trash, repairing streets, providing clean water, keeping the traffic lights working, and providing police, fire, and EMS services.  The work can be interesting, with good pay, great benefits, and opportunities for advancement.  

To be considered for one of these amazing opportunities, you may be required to pass a Civil Service exam.  The Civil Service Commission wants to prepare you as you enter into the City's hiring and selection process, by inviting you to attend the next Civil Service Testing Clinic.  

The testing clinic will provide insight into the history and purpose of the Civil Service Commission, an overview of the testing process from interest to eligible list, and a brief review of what to expect during the process. The target audience for course is anyone considering employment with the City of Columbus and/or taking a Civil Service exam.   

Spots are limited.

Click here to reserve your seat for the March 21st Civil Service Testing Clinic!

item.title: The City of Columbus is seeking Community Evaluators! Be the voice: Apply Today!
item.description:
The Community Gains a Voice in Selecting Police Officers and Firefighters

The City of Columbus is seeking Community Evaluators to evaluate job applicants for Police Officer and Firefighter.

Community Evaluators give the community a voice in the selection of City of Columbus Firefighters and Police Officers. During the journey to become a police officer or a firefighter, applicants take a video exam. During this exam, the applicants verbally respond to situations. Their responses are recorded for scoring at a later date. That’s where community evaluators come in. Community evaluators serve as a community representative on boards of three to evaluate and score the video-recorded applicant responses. Applicants who pass are placed on a list for consideration for hire.

Training:

 

As a community evaluator you will participate in training to learn what firefighters and police officers do. You will participate in a police officer ride-along. You will participate in evaluator training to learn about the scenarios, the evaluation criteria, and how to reduce biases while scoring. Then, you will be placed on a board with two other individuals, including a current police officer or firefighter. Before real scoring begins, the board will practice scoring candidates and receive coaching.

 

When:

 

Community evaluators need to be available on training and evaluation days. Below is a list of those dates. The asterisks symbolize the required dates. Community evaluators must also be available at least some of the other dates listed.

 

2024 Community Evaluator dates:

*Firefighter: Jan 25-Feb 9 (excluding Saturdays and Sundays)

*Police Officer: April 3-April 11(excluding Saturday and Sunday)

Police Officer: May 13-May 15

Police Officer: June 10-June 12

Police Officer: July 22-July 24

Police Officer: Aug 26-Aug28

Police Officer: Oct 7-Oct 10

Police Officer: Dec 3-Dec 5

Compensation for Service:

 

Community evaluators are compensated for their time as Independent Contractors. The contract allocates $200/day of service as a community evaluator (including training days).  Please note that OPERS retirees should consult OPERS before considering this opportunity.

 

Qualifications:

Community evaluators must have at least four years of professional experience which included hiring, evaluating, coaching, teaching, and/or counseling individuals or possession of a Bachelor's degree, and must be available all of the required days. Selected evaluators will be subject to a criminal background check. City employees are not eligible to serve as Community Evaluators.

 

How to be considered:

Apply through the City’s job page at www.governmentjobs.com/careers/columbusoh and select Community Evaluator (for Firefighter and Police Officer) (Vacancies). Complete the application no later than December 15, 2023.

Are you interested in employment with the City of Columbus, scheduled for a Civil Service exam, or just curious about the testing and selection process? 

Well, we have a course for you! 

The Civil Service Commission, in partnership with Citywide Training and Development (CTD) will host Civil Service Commission Testing Clinics each month from now through October 2023 to help you better prepare for the testing process. 

The remaining CSC Testing Clinic dates and times are as follows:

• Thursday, May 25, 2023 (2:00 PM-4:00 PM)
• Friday, June 2, 2023 (1:00 PM-3:00 PM)
• Tuesday, June 20, 2023 (2:00 PM-4:00 PM)
• Friday, July 7, 2023 (9:00 AM-11:00 AM)

• Friday, September 1, 2023 (9:00 AM-11:00 AM)
• Tuesday, September 19, 2023 (2:00 PM-4:00 PM)
• Friday, October 6, 2023 (1:00 PM-3:00 PM)
• Wednesday, October 25, 2023 (8:30 AM-10:30 AM)

These Testing Clinics are conveniently located at the Jerry Hammond Center, 1111 E. Broad Street Columbus, Ohio 43205.

Current City of Columbus employees can register for a Civil Service Commission Testing Clinic by logging into the Training Gateway.  If you are not a current City of Columbus employee, you can register by clicking here to complete the registration form. 

Email your completed registration form to CTD@Columbus.gov. 

Please note:  This is a FREE course.  Just enter your information, the date of the testing clinic that you would like to attend, and the course title: “Civil Service Commission Testing Clinic.”  

If you need assistance please do not hesitate to contact our offices at 614-645-8301.

item.title: City of Columbus - There's Still Time to Apply!
item.description:
Hello,

We kicked off January 2023 with the Opportunity Rising Career and Resource Fair, highlighting the hundreds of job vacancies in various city departments.  Hopefully, you had a chance to discuss the many employment opportunities, benefits, and programs, offered by the City of Columbus, with our dedicated city HR professionals.  

If you were not able to attend the Opportunity Rising Career and Resource Fair last month, no worries, there are still several positions available in a variety of career fields.  Anyone interested in a career with the City of Columbus is encouraged to create a job profile on our Civil Service Commission Website and submit an application.

On our website, you are able to:

  • Create and manage your job profile
  • Apply for job vacancies and Civil Service exams
  • View job classification details
  • Submit job alerts
  • Access employment guides and resources

Soon you will be able to register to attend a Civil Service Commission Testing Clinic on our website as well.  This course is for anyone considering employment with the City of Columbus, preparing to take a Civil Service exam, and/or wanting to better understand the city's testing and selection process.  Civil Service Commission Testing Clinics will begin in March 2023.        

As always, we are here for you!  If you have any questions, feel free to contact the Civil Service Commission office at 614-645-8301.

Thank you for your interest in employment with the City of Columbus!
